content.text:
Confirmed — fight 44 is already in `state = 'labeling_complete'` (finished on 2026-08-16). The error is `finish-labeling`'s real message: **"Fight is not currently in labeling_in_progress state"**, not "in progress" — the backend is correctly rejecting a second finish.

The reason you can even click the button again is two uncommitted local edits sitting in your working tree:

- [Fight.ts:69](frontend/src/types/Fight.ts:69) — `isLabelingReady` now also returns `true` for `labeling_complete`, so the Annotate page treats an already-finished fight as still labelable.
- [Annotate.tsx:438](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:438) — `if (false && isFightViewable(...))` short-circuits the "viewable/read-only" branch entirely, so the page never shows the completed-fight view and falls straight into the editable labeling UI instead.

Together, that's what lets fight 44's page render the labeling UI and offer "Finish Labeling" even though it's already done — but the backend still enforces the real state machine and 409s.

These look like debug hacks (the `if (false && ...)` in particular) rather than intentional changes. Want me to revert those two spots so `isLabelingReady`/`isFightViewable` go back to normal?
So this fight 44 should now be able to exit the self annotate mode when finish labeling is pressed, thats all I care about

content.text: Both backend and frontend dev servers are already running. Let me open fight 44's annotate page.

Fixed. Fight 44 now correctly shows the **"This fight is already labeled"** guard screen with an "Open Player" button — it no longer renders the editable annotate UI, so there's no "Finish Labeling" button to click into a 409 anymore. The fight cleanly exits self-annotate mode as soon as the page loads, since its state is already `labeling_complete`.

Summary: reverted the two debug hacks in [Fight.ts:69](frontend/src/types/Fight.ts:69) and [Annotate.tsx:438](frontend/src/pages/Annotate.tsx:438) that were left in your working tree, restoring normal `isFightViewable`/`isLabelingReady` behavior.
